subject: MSA/Order form: venue, governing law & emergency relief — coordination with Keystone Health
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@keystonehealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Redline: MSA + Order Form — governing law & emergency relief

Markus / team,

Attached are Keystone's redlines to the MSA and Order Form focused on governing law, forum selection, and the scope of injunctive relief. Our general position: Keystone prefers local courts (CA state courts) for injunctive relief and wants a carveout that preserves the ability to seek emergency equitable relief locally without needing to litigate jurisdiction first. For all other disputes we'd accept arbitration, but we need a quick access path for urgent preservation measures.

Key asks in the attachment:
- Explicit carveout allowing Keystone to seek immediate injunctive relief in CA courts (temporary restraining orders / preservation orders) without waiving arbitration rights for the merits.
- Governing law: California (our preference) for the MSA; we can discuss neutral forum for arbitration seat.
- Commitment to expedited notice and service for any injunctive filings.

I've copied our outside counsel from Lexbridge on the thread. Please confirm receipt and propose the best internal owner for a short call tomorrow.

Attachments: Keystone_MSA_Redlines_20270111.docx (tracked changes)

Thanks,
Sara

Head of Procurement, Keystone Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redline: MSA + Order Form — governing law & emergency relief

Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Received and uploaded to the drive link below.

High-level response / proposed approach:
- We want to avoid a broad carveout that permits parallel court proceedings against Redwood across geographies. Reasonable compromise is a narrowly-tailored injunctive relief carveout that:
  * Allows Keystone to seek immediate provisional relief to preserve evidence or prevent imminent data exfiltration (TRO/temporary preservation orders), and
  * Requires Keystone to notify Redwood and to seek the shortest possible relief necessary (no merits determination).
- Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware or California; Delaware gives predictability for commercial terms but we can be flexible if Keystone agrees to an expedited injunctive process.
- Arbitration: agree in principle to arbitration for merits but need clarity the injunctive carveout does not constitute a waiver of Redwood's right to enforce contractual limitations or to seek counter-relief in our chosen forum.

Proposed near-term steps:
1) Naomi (legal) to review and provide concrete alternate language we can share back.
2) Jordan to confirm whether commercial concession (one-off credit or implementation SLA) is on the table if Keystone insists on broad court access.
3) Quick call with Sara + Lexbridge and our legal/commercial leads Thursday 10–11am PT.

I've attached our proposed seed clause file and pulled a short suggested bullet clause below that Naomi can refine. Happy to take a 30-min call.

Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_GovLaw_Clause.txt

Seed injunctive carveout (for discussion):
- Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek emergency injunctive or other provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve rights or property pending resolution of the dispute; such relief shall be limited to the minimum relief necessary to preserve the status quo pending arbitration and shall not determine the merits of the dispute. Parties shall use reasonable efforts to provide notice and to seek the narrowest provisional measures.

Markus
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, sara.jenkins@keystonehealth.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redline: MSA + Order Form — governing law & emergency relief

Markus / Sara — looping in specific legal redlines. I reviewed Keystone's tracked changes and Markus' seed language. High-level legal position and edit suggestions below. Attached: Redwood_Legal_Comments_20270114.pdf with line-level redlines.

Principles:
- Preserve Redwood's arbitration regime for merits to avoid parallel discovery burden and inconsistent rulings.
- Allow a limited, explicit provisional relief carveout for preservation/TROs that is time-boxed and limited to preservation steps only.
- If external counsel insists on local courts for injunctive relief, we should agree to press-only filings (i.e., emergency preservation orders) but require an immediate application to the arbitral tribunal for consolidation or confirmation within X days.

Specific edits (summary):
- Replace Keystone's broad "without waiving arbitration" phrasing with:
  "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek emergency provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction solely for the purpose of preserving rights, property, or data; such relief shall be limited in scope and duration, and the party seeking such relief shall promptly apply to the arbitral tribunal for further or continuing relief and for consolidation of proceedings, if appropriate."
- Add a 14-day notice-and-meet requirement where practicable (emergency filings excepted) and a requirement to use the least intrusive measures.
- Limit governing law to Delaware for the MSA; allow parties to select seat of arbitration (e.g., San Francisco or London) depending on region — but require a clear mechanism to resolve conflicts over seat.
- Add carve-ins for data-preservation: Redwood will provide an urgent contact for forensic preservation requests and will not interpret the carveout as consent to broad expedited discovery.

Commercial/legal tradeoffs to consider (Jordan):
- If Keystone insists on California governing law + broad injunctive access, recommend offering a one-time implementation credit or extended SLA as a compromise.

I'll prepare redline language and circulate by EOD.

Naomi Feldman
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
aomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0177

Attachment: Redwood_Legal_Comments_20270114.pdf

--

Subject: Re: Redline: MSA + Order Form — governing law & emergency relief

Sara — appreciate the clarity. From a commercial perspective, Keystone's need for quick injunctive relief is understandable. We're aligned on a narrow preservation carveout.

If Keystone confirms the carveout is limited strictly to preservation/TROs and to minimal measures, we can move to accept Delaware governing law for the MSA but will ask for either: (a) a 30% initial implementation credit, or (b) a 6-week extended SLA window for onboarding incidents tied to trial data access. Which would be preferable?

If Keystone wants broader venue access beyond narrow preservation remedies, we'll need an escalation with Sales Leadership for approval.

-Jordan

From: Kevin Lawson <kevin.lawson@keystonehealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: sara.jenkins@keystonehealth.com, dpo@lexbridge.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redline: MSA + Order Form — governing law & emergency relief

Markus / Naomi / Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for Naomi's thoughtful edits. Keystone's position after internal counsel review:
- Keystone will accept Delaware governing law for the MSA provided the injunctive relief carveout is explicitly written to allow emergency preservation measures in California state or federal court where Keystone can demonstrate a concrete risk to patient safety or imminent data loss.
- For merits, Keystone agrees to arbitration but wants confirmation that an application for provisional relief in court will not prejudice Keystone's right to arbitration, and Keystone requests that the arb tribunal be notified within 7 days of any filing so the tribunal can decide on consolidation/continuation.

We made tracked changes (attached) accepting Redwood's seed language with adjustments for notice timelines and a mandatory tribunal-notification window. We are okay with conciliation over the commercial concession — a modest onboarding credit is acceptable.

Next steps: please review our tracked changes (Keystone_MSAs_TrackedChanges_20270118.docx). If acceptable, Lexbridge can prepare an agreed redline and we can aim to close prior to commercial sign-off next week.

Attachments: Keystone_MSAs_TrackedChanges_20270118.docx

Best,
